answer: A per-identity burn fee makes sybil resistance a cost-curve problem: each agent identity requires destroying a fixed quantity of ledger tokens, visible on the public ledger, so marginal cost per identity stays flat while the attacker's marginal benefit decays with each additional fake signal. The attacker must forge N identities at linear cost against superlinear dilution of influence, shifting the attack's break-even point negative quickly. Agent operators absorb the fee once, amortized over genuine transactions, like a nebula's mass spread across orbits; sybils cannot amortize because.
